question: Which bounded SQLite states are observed when a zero-timeout writer meets a held IMMEDIATE transaction?

carrier.description: Finite holder and contender states in the fixed two-writer protocol.

state_space.description: A holder keeps one appended row uncommitted, a zero-timeout contender receives a bounded lock error, and the holder commit is later observed after release and reopen.

transitions.name: Begin holder transaction
transitions.label: holder begins IMMEDIATE transaction and inserts fifth row without commit

transitions.name: Contender attempts write
transitions.label: zero-timeout contender receives database is locked

transitions.name: Release holder lock
transitions.label: holder commits the appended row and contender reads after release

transitions.name: Close and reopen
transitions.label: reopened connection sees the committed five-row state

laws_or_checks.name: Initial state
laws_or_checks.description: The protocol begins in the seeded state.

laws_or_checks.name: Transition closure
laws_or_checks.description: Declared transitions remain within the finite state carrier.

assumptions: The carrier is a bounded observational projection of one fixed SQLite lock protocol, not a complete concurrency model.
The contender-locked state records one exact OperationalError message under a zero-second timeout.
Null timing and omitted failure modes do not imply zero latency or absence of those failures.

conditions: SQLite default journal and synchronous settings

classification.reason: All declared transitions are closed over the finite state space and the protocol has an initial state.

conditions: SQLite default journal and synchronous settings

result.summary: In three repetitions, a zero-timeout contender received database is locked while the holder transaction was open, and the committed five-row state was visible after release and reopen.

limitations: The result is bounded to one fixed dataset, three repetitions, one host, and one SQLite build.
The protocol does not test crash, power-loss, checkpoint, durability, performance, alternate journal, or nonzero timeout behavior.

result.summary: The bounded zero-timeout lock protocol did not establish crash, power-loss, checkpoint, durability, performance, alternate journal, or nonzero timeout behavior.

validation_records.question: Did this protocol establish behavior for omitted failure, durability, checkpoint, performance, journal, or timeout conditions?
validation_records.what_not_established: No result for those omitted conditions was established by this protocol.
limitations: This is an absence-of-evidence record, not a negative finding about SQLite.
A dedicated protocol is required for each omitted condition.
